claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the trip ran 9.6 km against an optimal 3.9 km, +5.7 km (+144%), taking 26.5 min against an estimate of 7.7 min, so the ride was far longer than the direct Orchard Road → Marina Bay Sands route.

The track splits that excess into two off-route segments: 14:10–14:15 added 1.85 km (2.68 km driven vs 0.83 km optimal, up to 803 m off route) and 14:17–14:29 added 2.87 km (3.64 km driven vs 0.77 km optimal, up to 1553 m off route).

Neither segment is excused by road conditions: the only incident is an accident reported at 13:52 that sat on the optimal route itself (0 m from it) on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road, so it does not justify leaving that route, and the remaining traffic records are ordinary speed bands (Bras Basah 30–39 km/h, Bayfront 20–29 km/h) with fair weather.

The driver's claim of congestion is partly corroborated (Orchard Road speed band 1, 0–9 km/h, 14:00–14:10) but that alone cannot exempt a segment: RD-4(b) makes a speed band mere corroboration and requires a matching incident on the replaced part of the optimal route, and the only incident lay on the optimal route, not on the driver's detour.

The rider's consent reached no further than the named road Cavenagh: the rider answered the driver's "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" with "Sure" plus a request for a 7-Eleven stop (F11, 14:02), so at most the rider authorised driving along Cavenagh Road — and no fact in the record ties either off-route segment (F4, F5) to Cavenagh Road, so the actual path driven is undetermined rather than consented.

The 7-Eleven request was a stop, not a route change: the rider named no location (F11) and the driver chose a 7-Eleven on Beach Road (F14), roughly 2–3 km away, which is what produced the off-route track; under RD-3(b) a driver-chosen stop that creates an off-route segment is not excused merely because the rider asked to "stop", and the recorded 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (2995 m from pickup, 2098 m from drop-off, not a pickup/drop-off point) is that stop.

The driver's post-trip written statement that the rider verbally agreed to the wider routing is a statement only (F14), not consent: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the segment started, and the only rider message on the record is F11.

Because this was a metered RydeTAXI trip, the excess kilometres were billed: the fare shows 5.67 km of excess distance charged at $7.99 (5.67 × $1.41/km) inside a total of $25.81, with no surge (1.0×), so every unexcused detour kilometre was money the rider should not have paid.

The two unexcused off-route segments total 4.72 km (1.85 + 2.87), which at this trip's own rate of $1.41/km yields $6.66 to be refunded, and the separately billed mid-trip waiting time of $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) was clocked during the 14:20–14:24 stop, on a non-pickup, non-drop-off point where no published Ryde charge applies.

claims.assertion: The GPS track shows the trip ran 9.6 km against an optimal 3.9 km, +5.7 km (+144%), taking 26.5 min against an estimate of 7.7 min, so the ride was far longer than the direct Orchard Road → Marina Bay Sands route.

The track splits that excess into two off-route segments: 14:10–14:15 added 1.85 km (2.68 km driven vs 0.83 km optimal, up to 803 m off route) and 14:17–14:29 added 2.87 km (3.64 km driven vs 0.77 km optimal, up to 1553 m off route).

Neither segment is excused by road conditions: the only incident is an accident reported at 13:52 that sat on the optimal route itself (0 m from it) on Orchard Road towards Bras Basah after Cavenagh Road, so it does not justify leaving that route, and the remaining traffic records are ordinary speed bands (Bras Basah 30–39 km/h, Bayfront 20–29 km/h) with fair weather.

The driver's claim of congestion is partly corroborated (Orchard Road speed band 1, 0–9 km/h, 14:00–14:10) but that alone cannot exempt a segment: RD-4(b) makes a speed band mere corroboration and requires a matching incident on the replaced part of the optimal route, and the only incident lay on the optimal route, not on the driver's detour.

The rider's consent reached no further than the named road Cavenagh: the rider answered the driver's "ok if I go round by Cavenagh?" with "Sure" plus a request for a 7-Eleven stop (F11, 14:02), so at most the rider authorised driving along Cavenagh Road — and no fact in the record ties either off-route segment (F4, F5) to Cavenagh Road, so the actual path driven is undetermined rather than consented.

The 7-Eleven request was a stop, not a route change: the rider named no location (F11) and the driver chose a 7-Eleven on Beach Road (F14), roughly 2–3 km away, which is what produced the off-route track; under RD-3(b) a driver-chosen stop that creates an off-route segment is not excused merely because the rider asked to "stop", and the recorded 4 min 10 s stationary period at 14:20–14:24 (2995 m from pickup, 2098 m from drop-off, not a pickup/drop-off point) is that stop.

The driver's post-trip written statement that the rider verbally agreed to the wider routing is a statement only (F14), not consent: consent must be the rider's own message sent before the segment started, and the only rider message on the record is F11.

Because this was a metered RydeTAXI trip, the excess kilometres were billed: the fare shows 5.67 km of excess distance charged at $7.99 (5.67 × $1.41/km) inside a total of $25.81, with no surge (1.0×), so every unexcused detour kilometre was money the rider should not have paid.

The two unexcused off-route segments total 4.72 km (1.85 + 2.87), which at this trip's own rate of $1.41/km yields $6.66 to be refunded, and the separately billed mid-trip waiting time of $1.08 (4.2 min × $0.26/min) was clocked during the 14:20–14:24 stop, on a non-pickup, non-drop-off point where no published Ryde charge applies.

The driver has 3 disputes with 1 upheld in the last 90 days and 812 trips, so this upheld route deviation makes the conduct repeated and warrants sending the account for Ryde review alongside the refund.
The driver also ignored a second rider message asking him to turn back.

The rider's "Sure" (F11) can be read as a general route authorisation to avoid Orchard congestion, which under RD-5 covers route choice made for reaching the destination; the driver will argue this reaches both segments (F4, F5), whereas I argue it is limited to Cavenagh Road and undetermined for the rest — the finding could be undetermined and referred to a human under G13.
